page: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processors delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores at speeds up to 4.5 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory system is configured with 256.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per thread. An integrated local storage array provides 3,780 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD capacity, while GPU accelerators are absent.

Benchmark evaluations position the instance in the top tier (top 10%) for single-core execution with a stress-ng score of 3,766.97 and a PassMark CPU score of 94,549.31. Multi-threaded capacity remains strong in the top 25%, demonstrating 118,560.52 in stress-ng and 105,850.51 in extended instructions tests, accelerated by instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16. Memory bandwidth registers 205.9 GB/sec read and 132.81 GB/sec write for uncached 256MB blocks, driving top-tier PassMark database operations at 36,882.3 and 102.79 million Redis SET operations per second.

Without dedicated GPU hardware, large-scale deep learning execution encounters predictable throughput constraints. While small and medium language model inferences execute within top-tier bands—such as 4,989.67 prompt tokens per second on 135M models and 44.15 generation tokens per second on 7B models—scaling to 70B parameter models drops performance to average percentiles (4.7 generation tokens per second).

Combining dense compute cores, fast multi-threaded data decompression, and 3,780 GB of low-latency local NVMe storage, the D64ads_v7 provides strong resource efficiency for data pipelines, large in-memory caching layers, relational database servers, and concurrent static web workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores) and 256.0 GB of memory. It includes 3,780 GB of direct NVMe SSD local storage without hardware GPU accelerators. The instance exhibits top-tier benchmark results across single-core processing (stress-ng score of 3,766.97), PassMark CPU operations (94,549.31), and database workloads (36,882.3), backed by AVX-512 and VNNI vector instruction sets. Memory throughput reaches 205.9 GB/sec for uncached read blocks, facilitating 102.79 million Redis SET operations per second and strong static web delivery. While CPU-based lightweight LLM inference runs capably, larger 70B models show baseline throughput tradeoffs. This hardware profile provides a balanced, high-density environment optimized for relational databases, Redis caching, compression workflows, and data processing.
